title: Quentin and the Oath
premise: Lena Nakamura has spent seven years copying prayers no god answers, hiding their gift for hearing the dead in the margins of temple ledgers. When the old gods of Thornfell stir awake, the debt-masters who own Lena's contract realize what they have—and so does the thing wearing King Aldric's crown, a devouring spirit that eats memories to stay alive. Fleeing with a disgraced oath-keeper named Quentin and a smuggler found-family who owe them nothing and give everything anyway, Lena must reach the mountain shrine where the first oath was sworn. To unbind the king, someone must feed the crown every memory they possess; Lena pays that price, and wakes with nothing but the family who refuses to let them be forgotten.
about_author: Cyrus Okafor is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial-era records before turning to fiction about power, paper, and who gets remembered. They write from a small house at the edge of a real mountain range, where the weather does most of the plotting.

chapters.title: Ink That Listens
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the temple scriptorium, Lena copies a prayer that answers itself back—a voice in the dried ink. They hide the page, terrified their secret gift has been noticed. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by longing, the ache of being unseen.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Debt-master Corvane summons Lena, revealing he knows about the answered prayer and doubles their bond-price overnight. A smuggler named Sefa watches the exchange from the doorway. Beat: claustrophobic injustice, the cage made visible.

chapters.title: The King Who Forgot His Daughter
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Oath-keeper Quentin, exiled for accusing the king of being 'worn,' witnesses Princess Isolde visit a father who doesn't know her name. He resolves to act. Beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Roads Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa guides a disguised Quentin over the passes, trading gossip about a scribe who hears the dead. Beat: wry warmth, the smugglers' code of debts honored more honestly than kings' laws.

chapters.title: What the Margins Say
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Old marginalia in a forbidden codex describe the Oath of Unbinding—the only rite that can strip a possessing spirit. The ink-voice whispers a warning: the crown is coming for the temple archives. Beat: discovery laced with fear.

chapters.title: Sold to the Crown
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Corvane sells Lena's contract to royal agents hunting anyone touched by the old gods. Lena flees through the scriptorium's hidden stair as soldiers burn the archive behind them. Beat: panic, loss of the only home they knew.

chapters.title: A Smuggler's Mercy
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa finds Lena half-frozen on the pass and takes them in against her better judgment. The crew argues; gruff cook Bram votes last, and his yes settles it. Beat: reluctant shelter becoming the seed of belonging.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At court, Quentin confronts the king privately; the thing inside speaks with Aldric's mouth, reciting Quentin's own forgotten childhood back at him. Beat: horror and the terrible intimacy of being known by your enemy.

chapters.title: Names Are Rations
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Around the fire, Lena explains how the crown-spirit feeds on memory—villages forget their dead, soldiers forget why they fight. The crew realizes whole valleys have gone blank. Beat: dawning scale of the threat.

chapters.title: The Hollow Village
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The crew passes a village where no one remembers their own children's faces. Bram, who grew up there, finds his mother alive and a stranger to him. Beat: heartbreak; the cost of the crown made personal.

chapters.title: Isolde's Bargain
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The princess, suspecting what wears her father, secretly hires Sefa's crew to smuggle her out—she carries a fragment of the true coronation oath. Beat: wary alliance, two fugitives recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Switchback
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Royal wardens ambush the caravan on a cliff road; Lena's knowledge of smuggler turns saves them, but Sefa takes a wound. Beat: adrenaline giving way to trust earned in blood.

chapters.title: The Ink-Voice Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The voice in Lena's blood reveals itself: it is Vesh, last priest of the old gods, bound into the mountain when the crown was forged. It names the shrine's location—and warns the rite demands a memory-price. Beat: revelation and foreboding.

chapters.title: Quentin's Broken Word
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin confesses he once swore an oath to protect the king and failed, which is why the exile-brand burns him. Lena tells him oaths can be re-sworn differently. Beat: shame met with grace.

chapters.title: The Salt Market
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Resupplying in a free-town, the crew learns Corvane has posted a bounty and wardens are questioning everyone. A child informer nearly betrays them; Isolde buys silence with her ring. Beat: tension, moral compromise.

chapters.title: What Isolde Remembers
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde shares her last clear memory of her father—teaching her to fly a kite before the crown changed him. The fragment-oath she carries is written in his hand. Beat: tenderness as fuel for the fight ahead.

chapters.title: The Warden's Net
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Captured briefly by warden-captain Hale, Lena bargains: they'll read the crown's true name from a relic if Hale lets the others go. Hale hesitates—he has begun forgetting his son. Beat: enemy humanized, escape bought with risk.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Storm-trapped in a cave, the crew trades stories instead of secrets; Lena, for the first time, speaks of the parents sold away to cover their debt. Beat: found family solidifying around a fire.

chapters.title: Vesh's History Lesson
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vesh shows Lena visions: the old gods were not worshipped but contracted, and the crown was built to enslave them. Power corrupted its makers first. Beat: thematic deepening—power devours its holders.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Corvane catches up, offering to tear up Lena's debt if they hand over Isolde. Lena refuses—and Corvane reveals he sold their parents' contract to the crown years ago. Beat: rage and severance; the old cage broken for good.

chapters.title: The Shrine Gate
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The crew reaches the sealed shrine; it opens only to a freely-sworn oath. Quentin swears himself to Lena's quest, and the exile-brand cools. Beat: redemption's first breath.

chapters.title: Trials of the First Priests
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Inside, three trials test the party: a door that opens to a truth spoken aloud, a bridge that holds only shared weight, a dark that shows each person their worst memory. Beat: unity forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vesh explains the unbinding: the crown must be fed a complete life willingly given—every memory, freely poured out—or it will simply take a kingdom instead. Beat: dread crystallizing into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Volunteers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, braided. Each crew member privately offers themselves; each is refused—the rite needs someone who can hear the dead to pour the memories out. Everyone understands what that means for Lena. Beat: love expressed as argument.

chapters.title: Hale's Choice
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Warden-captain Hale arrives with troops—but having forgotten his son's face, he chooses to hold the pass against the crown's reinforcements instead. Beat: a broken man reclaiming himself.

chapters.title: March on the Capital
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The company descends toward the capital as the crown-spirit accelerates its feeding; whole districts wake not knowing their own names. Beat: urgency, a city dissolving.

chapters.title: Into the Palace Dark
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Using Isolde's knowledge and smuggler routes, they infiltrate the palace through the old god-tunnels beneath it. Beat: suspense, the past literally underfoot.

chapters.title: Aldric, Beneath
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Deep in the king's mind-prison, Isolde reaches the real Aldric, who clings to one memory: the kite. She anchors him with it. Beat: hope kindled in the darkest place.

chapters.title: Corvane's End
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Corvane, trying to bargain with the crown for power, is consumed by it—his memories stripped in seconds. Lena watches the fate meant for them. Beat: horror as cautionary mirror.

chapters.title: The Throne Room
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Confrontation: Quentin re-swears his broken oath—not to the crown but to the man beneath it—and the words bind the spirit's attention. Beat: courage as keeping faith differently.

chapters.title: The Pouring Out
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Climax begins: Lena kneels before the crown and begins giving everything—every memory, offered freely while Vesh channels them through the first oath. Beat: sacrifice rendered intimate, memory by memory.

chapters.title: What the Crown Took
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Inside the feeding, Lena experiences the spirit's own origin—it was once a person who took power to stop being hurt. Lena pities it even as they starve it. Beat: compassion at the edge of annihilation.

chapters.title: Unbound
chapters.summary: Braided POVs. The crown cracks; Aldric collapses free, weeping his daughter's name; the old gods' contracts dissolve into simple gratitude. But Lena lies empty-eyed among the shards. Beat: triumph shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Lena wakes knowing nothing—not their name, not the faces around the bed. The crew begins telling them their own story, piece by piece. Beat: devastation held by tenderness.

chapters.title: Relearning Lena
chapters.summary: Multi-POV vignettes. Sefa teaches the mountain roads again; Quentin reads them Lena's own journal; Isolde brings the recovered marginalia. Some things return; some don't. Beat: patience as devotion.

chapters.title: The Kite
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Regent-for-now Isolde restores the old contracts as covenants, not chains. She gives Lena a kite made from the shrine's banner-cloth. Beat: renewal, institutions mended by memory kept honest.

chapters.title: Debt Forgiven
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena discovers the new government burned all debt-ledgers—including theirs. Standing in the ash, they feel the first flicker of a returned memory: Sefa's fire, Bram's stew. Beat: freedom arriving quietly.

chapters.title: The Voice in New Ink
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Copying the new covenant, Lena hears a faint voice—not Vesh, something younger, curious. Their gift survived the emptying, changed. Beat: wonder reborn, identity as ongoing creation.

chapters.title: Oath Renewed
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin formally swears his keeper's oath anew—to Lena, to the crew, to the covenant. The brand fades to a pale scar he stops hiding. Beat: restoration, chosen bonds over imposed ones.

chapters.title: Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the anniversary, the found family climbs to the shrine together. Lena still can't remember the day they saved a kingdom—but they remember this: every face beside them, and choosing it daily. Beat: warm resolution; memory lives in those who carry you.
